lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: Exit 13. Middle of nowhere on Highway 13.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: Night auditor. That's what they call it. Fancy name for 'the person who sits here from 10 PM to 6 AM while the world sleeps.'

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: The pay is enough. The quiet is... welcome. After everything.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: Clock in at the register. Read the shift notes. Check the motel board. Simple.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: This is just a gas station. Just a motel. Just a job.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: ...Right.

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: Hey. Just need twenty on pump two and a coffee.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: Sure. That'll be—

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: Long drive. Haven't seen another car for miles. This the only stop between here and the county line?

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: Only one I know of.

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: Figures. Place has that look. Like it's been here longer than the road.

lines.speaker: Guest
lines.text: I'd like Room 4, please.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: Room 4 is... unavailable. It's been closed.

lines.speaker: Guest
lines.text: Closed? I stayed in Room 4 last time I was here. Nice room. Quiet.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: When was that?

lines.speaker: Guest
lines.text: Oh... recently. I think. The drive blurs together after a while.

choices.text: I can put you in Room 2 instead.
Room 4 has been boarded up for years. Who are you?
No rooms available. You should keep driving.

lines.speaker: Radio
lines.text: [static] ...requesting assistance... vehicle... Mile 87...

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: What the—

lines.speaker: Radio
lines.text: [static] ...multiple vehicles... road conditions... [static]

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: That frequency... that's a dispatch channel. Why is the CB picking up dispatch?

lines.speaker: Radio
lines.text: [static] ...Room 4 is ready... [static]

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: That's not dispatch. That was—who said that?

lines.speaker: Deputy Hale
lines.text: Evening. Deputy Hale, county sheriff's office. Just doing a wellness check on the property.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: Everything's fine here.

lines.speaker: Deputy Hale
lines.text: Yeah, I'm sure. Listen, we've had some reports. Travelers calling in about this location. Saying things aren't... right.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: What kind of things?

lines.speaker: Deputy Hale
lines.text: People checking in who don't check out. Cars in the lot that aren't registered. CCTV footage that doesn't match the logs. Normal stuff for a place like this, usually. But the frequency is... unusual.

lines.speaker: Deputy Hale
lines.text: You notice anything strange?

choices.text: The radio picks up old dispatch calls. I think something happened at Mile 87.
Nothing strange. Just a quiet job.
You should check the basement. And Room 4.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: The ledger doesn't add up. Three check-ins last night that I don't remember processing.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: Room 1: Martinez. Room 3: Chen. Room 5: Okafor.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: I checked in one person last night. One. And it wasn't any of these names.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: But the key cards were issued. The timestamps are there. In my handwriting.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: ...In my handwriting.

lines.speaker: Radio
lines.text: [clearer now] Dispatch, this is Unit 7. We have a multi-vehicle collision at Mile 87. Requesting all available—

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: That's the call. That's the exact call from the pileup three years ago.

lines.speaker: Radio
lines.text: [static] —eleven confirmed casualties, road completely blocked—

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: I was on duty that night. I was the dispatcher who took that call.

lines.speaker: Radio
lines.text: [static] —exit options limited, nearest service plaza is Exit 13—

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: They were sent here. The survivors were directed to Exit 13.

lines.speaker: Radio
lines.text: [static] —how many survivors?— [long pause] —define 'survivor'—

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: ...What does that mean?

lines.speaker: Ranger Moss
lines.text: County ranger. Perimeter looks fine outside. You the night auditor?

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: That's me.

lines.speaker: Ranger Moss
lines.text: Word of advice. This stretch of highway has a history. Lots of breakdowns, lots of stranded folks. Most of them just need gas and a bed.

lines.speaker: Ranger Moss
lines.text: But some of them... they don't quite fit. You know what I mean?

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: I'm starting to.

lines.speaker: Ranger Moss
lines.text: Don't dig too deep. The people who dig too deep end up staying. And I don't mean as employees.

lines.speaker: Phone (D. Harlan)
lines.text: Velez. It's Harlan. We need to talk.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: I'm listening.

lines.speaker: Phone (D. Harlan)
lines.text: You've been going through the archive. You've been asking the deputy questions. You've been listening to that radio.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: I've been doing my job.

lines.speaker: Phone (D. Harlan)
lines.text: Your job is to run the register and check in guests. That's it. The history of this place is not your concern.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: People are checking in who shouldn't exist, Harlan. The ledger writes itself. The radio plays dispatch calls from three years ago.

lines.speaker: Phone (D. Harlan)
lines.text: And the business has never been better. Think about that. Revenue is up. The motel is full. The pumps are running. Exit 13 is profitable for the first time in a decade. You want to keep your job and your paycheck? Stop digging.

choices.text: Fine. I'll focus on the work.
Something is wrong here and you know it. I'm going to find out what.
The revenue comes from dead customers, Harlan. You're profiting off ghosts.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: The basement. Finally.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: Filing cabinets. Decades of them. Guest logs going back to... 1987? Earlier?

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: Wait. These names. Martinez. Chen. Okafor. They're in the 1987 logs. The 1995 logs. The 2003 logs. The 2019 logs.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: Same names. Same rooms. Same check-in times. Over and over and over.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: And here—the original accident report. Mile 87. Not three years ago. The first one was in 1987. Same stretch of road. Same number of casualties. Same... exit.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: Exit 13 isn't just near Mile 87. It IS Mile 87. It's where they come.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: Every accident on that stretch of highway... the dead end up here. Checking in. Buying coffee. Pumping gas. Like nothing happened.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: And someone has been running the register for them. For forty years.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: I know what this place is now. A waystation. For the lost.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: The highway keeps them moving. The plaza gives them somewhere to stop. And the night auditor... processes them through.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: But why me? Why did I take this job?

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: The pileup three years ago. I was the dispatcher. I heard them die. Eleven people.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: And then I had the breakdown. And then I came here.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: Was it coincidence? Or was I sent here too?

lines.speaker: Radio Voice
lines.text: Mara.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: You again.

lines.speaker: Radio Voice
lines.text: You found the archive. You understand now.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: I understand that Exit 13 collects the dead from Mile 87 and someone profits from it.

lines.speaker: Radio Voice
lines.text: Not collects. Holds. The highway is a loop, Mara. Mile 87 to Exit 13 and back. The people who die there don't move on. They circle. They stop. They leave. They circle again.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: And the owner knows.

lines.speaker: Radio Voice
lines.text: The owner built the business around it. Every transaction, every room night, every gallon of gas—it anchors them here. Keeps the loop running. Keeps the revenue flowing.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: How do I stop it?

lines.speaker: Radio Voice
lines.text: You have to choose. Keep the station open and the dead stay comfortable but trapped. Shut it down and they face what's at the end of the road. Or...

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: Or what?

lines.speaker: Radio Voice
lines.text: Or you find out why YOU were really sent here. And that changes everything.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: The room logs. The financial records. The dispatch tapes. The accident reports.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: I have everything. The question is what I do with it.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: Harlan profits from the loop. The deputy looks the other way. The radio voice wants me to break it.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: And the guests... they don't even know they're dead. They just want coffee and a room for the night.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: What do I owe them? Protection? Truth? Freedom? Or just good service?

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: Last shift. Everything I've done, every choice I've made, it all comes down to tonight.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: The storm is the worst it's ever been. Every room is booked. Every pump is running. The radio won't stop.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: And Room 4... is open.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: I didn't open it. But it's open.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: Time to clock in. One last time.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: I walked away. The plaza is still there. The pumps still run. The motel sign still glows.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: Someone else will take the night shift. Someone else will process the guests who shouldn't be traveling.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: I know part of the truth now. Not all of it. Maybe not even most of it.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: But I know enough to keep driving. Past Mile 87. Past Exit 13. Into whatever morning looks like when you've spent your nights with the dead.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: The highway stretches out ahead. Long and dark and empty.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: But at least I'm moving.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: The money is good. Better than good.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: Harlan was right. The business has never been more profitable. Full motel. Busy pumps. Coffee flowing all night.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: So what if the customers are dead? They pay. They tip. They don't complain much.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: I upgraded the cameras. Fixed the generator. Repaired the laundry. Exit 13 has never looked better.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: The radio still plays sometimes. The dispatch calls. The names. I turn it down now.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: Clock in. Serve the customers. Balance the till. Go home. Come back.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: This is my life now. And honestly?

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: The night shift isn't so bad when you stop asking questions.

lines.speaker: Radio
lines.text: [static]

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: I have to understand. I have to know everything. Every name. Every accident. Every loop.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: The archive goes deeper than I thought. Sub-basements. Old tunnels under the highway.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: I stopped sleeping. Stopped going home. The apartment feels wrong now. Too quiet. Too far from the station.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: The guests recognize me now. Not as the auditor. As one of them.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: I check the motel board. My name is there. Room 4. Checked in.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: When did I—

lines.speaker: Radio
lines.text: [static] —requesting assistance... vehicle... Mile 87... one casualty... dispatcher on duty: M. Velez—

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: Oh.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: I see.

lines.speaker: Radio
lines.text: [static fades to silence]

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: I know what happened. All of it.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: Mile 87 is a wound in the highway. Exit 13 was built on top of it. The loop keeps the dead moving so they never have to face the end.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: And me? I was the dispatcher who heard them die. The guilt brought me here. The loop tried to keep me.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: But I have all the evidence. Every name. Every date. Every lie.

lines.speaker: Radio Voice
lines.text: Mara. It's time.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: I know.
[Mara walks to Room 4. The door is open. Inside: not a room. A stretch of highway. Night. Rain. Headlights approaching.]

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: I remember now. The call. The pileup. I wasn't just the dispatcher.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: I was driving home that night. After my shift. Through the rain. Past Mile 87.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: And I—
[The headlights. The impact. The silence. And then—]
[Morning. The storm has passed. The plaza is empty. The sign reads 'CLOSED'. The pumps are dark. The motel doors stand open.]
[On the counter: a shift log. One final entry.]
[All guests checked out. No charges. Have a safe drive.]
[Signed: Mara Velez, Night Auditor, Exit 13.]
[The highway stretches empty in both directions. The sun rises. The loop is broken.]
[The dead are free. And so is Mara.]
